notes:
Speccify 0.9.4 brings actions and event automation into one shared workflow.

- Define an action once with named inputs, then run it manually, through the Exec MCP or from an approved Spec event.
- Review exact invocations and confirm automation risks locally. Approval applies to the unchanged source configuration; new or changed automation needs manual approval. External Desktop MCP clients can propose changes but cannot approve them.
- Use Codex Queue, independent Claude Print sessions or local program actions with the same explicit input contract.
- Review project migration after updates and before new agent sessions. Safe migrations preserve existing definitions and customized files; CLI installation or repair remains an explicit action.
- See clear action-form validation and save results. Folding the right sidebar also hides its docked terminal while preserving the session and output.

Update or install:

- Published 0.8.8 or later: Environment → Updates → download → install and restart. Save outstanding edits and resolve restart checks first. No Beta opt-in is needed for this stable release.
- Published 0.8.7 or earlier: install once from the download page; those versions use the former private update feed.
- Linux deb/rpm: update through the package manager. In-app Linux updates apply to AppImage.

Targets: macOS Apple Silicon, Windows x64, Linux x86_64 and Linux arm64. macOS packages are Developer ID signed and notarized. Windows Authenticode signing is not configured, so SmartScreen may warn; update-package signatures are checked independently on all four targets.

Validation includes 403 frontend tests, 423 Rust tests (three ignored), 412 Python tests (one deselected) and all 33 desktop browser scripts. Typechecking, formatting, CI lint and documentation checks passed. The additional strict desktop Clippy check retains 15 pre-existing findings. Native development checks exercised disposable projects and a harmless local action; no real Codex or Claude account work was submitted. Interactive Windows/Linux installation and the productive macOS 0.9.3-to-0.9.4 update transition remain separate checks.

Release guide: https://speccify.io/releases/0-9-4/
Download: https://speccify.io/download/
